newsitem.title: USA: US money managers turn defensive on US debt -- MCM.
newsitem.headline: US money managers turn defensive on US debt -- MCM.

text.p: Fixed-income managers became more defensive on U.S. debt markets in the past week, said the latest MCM MoneyWatch Inc asset allocation survey.
Investors are "clearly slightly more defensive," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague. "This group appears to be hiding in (the) belly of (the yield) curve."
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark slipped to 105.6 in the week ended August 26 from 106.1 percent in the prior week.

A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market. A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 22 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," down from 24 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 19 percent, up from 9.0 percent in the week ended August 19.
Fifty-nine percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, down from 67 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets rose to 3.12 percent, against 3.02 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 32 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, down from 39 percent in the previous week, while 39 percent underweighted it. The remaining 29 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 36 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 21 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants, who manage about $90.0 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM.
